target_customer: Small businesses and teams wanting a private, self-hosted collaboration server
problem: Small teams depend on centralized cloud services for file sharing and chat and want to own their data without running servers themselves.
business_model: Hardware box sale with bundled collaboration software and no monthly fees
product_category: Private cloud server hardware with collaboration software

founders.name: Ali Jelveh
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; announced the 2017 insolvency filing per Deutsche Startups.

exit.reason: Insolvency filed in Hamburg in February 2017; a May 2017 headline reported a takeover was in sight; the company site protonet.com still operates

technical_complexity.rationale: Combined custom server hardware, a Linux-based collaboration software stack, encryption and remote backups for non-technical customers.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware-plus-software bundle was differentiated against SaaS but easy for NAS makers like Synology and QNAP to approach.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: NAS vendors and cloud suites dominated the category; no dated source shows them acting against Protonet specifically.

market_need_then: German crowd investors funded Protonet quickly in 2012 and 2014 (over 1 million euros in about 3.5 hours in June 2014), showing strong early enthusiasm for private cloud alternatives.

branding.domain_note: Moved from protonet.info (YC listing) to protonet.com; no source on acquisition or date.

identity.logo: Red, silver and white logo per a logo catalog
identity.voice_and_tone: Privacy and ownership framing, encryption as strong as online banking

branding.community_and_virality: German press called it startup of the year 2013 and covered the Seedmatch records; thousands of crowd investors received product vouchers.

brand_strength.rationale: Unusually well known in German startup press due to crowdfunding records, though confusable with Proton (ProtonMail) and the insolvency damaged it.

outcome_analysis: Protonet raised roughly 3 million euros from German crowd investors across 2012 and 2014 and shipped private cloud boxes, but filed for insolvency in Hamburg in February 2017 and told customers to move to their own domains. A May 2017 headline said a takeover was in sight and protonet.com still operates, so it survived in some form. The sources found do not give a detailed cause beyond running out of money.
notes: Funding amounts come from search result summaries because direct page fetches of the crowdfund article returned 403: about 200,000 euros on Seedmatch in 2012, over 1 million euros in June 2014 and about 3 million euros total per Deutsche Startups (3.2 million as cited in another snippet). These were in euros and are not converted, so amount_usd is null. CB Insights lists 3.29M USD over 5 rounds with Y Combinator and Startplatz as investors; unverified. Seedmatch deals were participating subordinated loans, not equity. Takeover buyer and outcome not confirmed; status Active on YC while insolvency occurred, so exit type is unknown. protonet.info redirects to protonet.com, which was not fetched. Competitor list left empty: only undated or current-day NAS articles found. Founder bios not found.
